gappers.catalyst: Bloom Energy shares surged after a Q2 2026 earnings beat and raised full-year guidance.
headlines: Bloom Energy shares surged following strong Q2 earnings results and raised full-year guidance
gappers.catalyst_detail: Bloom Energy reported record Q2 2026 revenue of $1.065B (first quarter above $1B, +165.5% YoY, $935.4M product revenue) and raised FY2026 guidance to $3.9-4.2B revenue with ~34% non-GAAP gross margin and $800-900M operating income. Also announced an expanded $25B financing partnership with Brookfield (up from $5B), a strategic Oracle agreement for up to 2.8GW of fuel cell deployment for AI infrastructure, and a $1.7B project investment from Industrial Development Funding/Oaktree tied to Nebius AI infra.
gappers.why: Earnings beat plus raised guidance pulls in momentum buyers; layered on top of a structural AI-datacenter power-demand narrative (Oracle, Nebius deals) rather than a single-metric beat, which broadens the buyer base beyond quant/momentum flow.
gappers.impact: Gappers-alpaca.sh has no true premarket-volume field; the 1,007,762 figure is the prior completed session's full-day volume, clears the routine's 50k floor easily but isn't a same-day conviction read. Multiple concurrent, dollar-quantified catalysts (guidance raise + Brookfield + Oracle + Nebius/Oaktree) argue against a single-headline spike; no other watchlist name moved in sympathy today, so this reads BE-specific rather than sector-wide.
gappers.horizon: LONG_TERM, structural growth drivers (raised guidance, multi-billion financing/hyperscaler commitments for AI power) align with Bloom Energy's Energy-sector fuel-cell thesis already on WATCHLIST.md, not a one-day headline fade.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Account is flat (0 open positions, weekly trade count 0/3 per Jul 28 EOD log), so this displaces nothing directly. Taking it would use 1 of 3 weekly trade slots and up to 20% of equity; BE is highly volatile post-gap, so the entry stop distance needs sizing (scripts/size.mjs) before a 2:1 R:R can be confirmed — not assessed here, this is research only.

gappers.catalyst: Share buybacks and a $61.4M note redemption failed to reverse declining momentum; shares fell further amid ongoing weakness.
headlines: BW Investors Weigh Buybacks, Debt Redemption And Weak Momentum
gappers.catalyst_detail: Babcock & Wilcox reported Q1 2026 revenue of $214.4M (+42.55% vs consensus, +44% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $16.1M (+296% YoY), with net debt down to 0.42x TTM EBITDA. Despite this, shares are down ~33% over the past 30 days ($14.45 on Jun 26 to $9.62 by Jul 24) on multiple securities class-action lawsuits alleging undisclosed related-party ties to largest shareholder BRC Group Holdings. Company plans to redeem all $61.4M of its 6.50% Senior Notes on Aug 13, 2026 and authorized a $50M buyback to start after the Q2 10-Q filing.
gappers.why: Litigation overhang (undisclosed related-party allegations) is dominating price action despite a strong operating quarter and debt paydown — governance/legal risk outweighing fundamentals in the market's read.
gappers.impact: Not a one-day spike — this is a continuation of an existing 30-day, ~33% decline; today's -7.34% is a fresh leg down, not an isolated headline event. Volume is thin (30.6K, prior full-session) consistent with a small/illiquid name. No clear sector read-through — company-specific legal risk.
gappers.horizon: SHORT_TERM in the sense that the trend is still actively deteriorating with no resolution catalyst; litigation risk has no defined end date, so there's no basis for a swing-hold thesis right now.
gappers.opportunity_cost: 0/6 positions open, 0/3 weekly trades used — no existing holding displaced. But an active, unresolved securities-fraud litigation overhang plus a still-falling 30-day trend fails the Entry Checklist's clean-catalyst bar; this reads as a re-test of broken support, not a fresh setup. Skip.

gappers.catalyst: onsemi (ON Semiconductor) agreed to acquire Synaptics in an all-stock deal; some analysts downgraded the stock following the announcement.
headlines: onsemi to Acquire Synaptics in $6.2-7B All-Stock Deal
gappers.catalyst_detail: onsemi agreed to acquire Synaptics in an all-stock transaction valued at ~$7B enterprise value. Synaptics holders receive 1.350 onsemi shares per SYNA share (~19% premium to the 10-day VWAP), implying ~12% pro forma ownership of the combined company. Deal targets ~$200M in synergies (85-90% opex/SG&A) and is expected to be non-GAAP EPS-accretive within 18 months of closing, with close expected mid-2027 pending shareholder and regulatory approval.
gappers.why: Classic M&A repricing — an announced acquisition at a premium pulls the target toward deal value. Because consideration is all-stock (not cash), SYNA now also trades as a partial proxy for onsemi's own stock, which is why some analysts downgraded (loses standalone upside, adds onsemi execution/integration risk).
gappers.impact: Durable, not a headline spike — this is a signed, SEC-filed merger agreement, not a rumor; the repricing should hold barring a deal break or topping bid. Today's semiconductor tape is otherwise weak (KLIC and broader semis down on sector-wide pressure), so this move is stock-specific M&A, not sector momentum.
gappers.horizon: LONG_TERM/structural (signed M&A) but on an ~11-month timeline to close (mid-2027) — this is effectively a merger-arbitrage position now, not a momentum swing trade; the strategy's swing-hold framing doesn't cleanly apply.
gappers.opportunity_cost: No displacement needed (0/6 open, 0/3 weekly). Entering into the announcement pop has capped upside (bounded by the fixed 1.35x exchange ratio) and full downside on deal break — asymmetric and unfavorable vs. this strategy's momentum setups; unlikely to clear a clean 2:1 R:R and falls outside the current playbook (momentum/breakout, not merger-arb). Skip unless operator explicitly wants to run arb.
